page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for distributed deep learning and large-scale parallel processing. The server features four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM. It is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 8481C processors running on the x86_64 architecture, providing 52 physical cores and 104 vCPUs clocked at 2.7 GHz. The compute layer includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX instructions for INT8 and Bfloat16 operations.

System memory consists of 936.0 GB of RAM, offering approximately 9.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a high-speed 3216 GB NVMe SSD array, which supports low-latency data staging for large datasets. In memory benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-quartile performance, sustaining 216.58 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB read operations and 6842.06 GB/sec across cached small blocks. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating private networking or dedicated IP allocation.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier capabilities across parallel and compute-heavy metrics. The host achieved a PassMark CPU score of 86938.94 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 19675.0, both placing in the upper performance tiers. Vector processing capabilities are emphasized by top-decile Geekbench image processing scores of 18479.0 and strong compiler throughput. In inference benchmarks, text generation yields 38.11 tokens per second on a medium 7B model and 4.61 tokens per second on a large 70B parameter model.

The dense pairing of four H100 GPUs, 3216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and extensive host memory creates an efficient environment for complex training and serving workloads without provisioning separate hardware clusters. While single-thread CPU benchmarks place in the average tier, the machine compensates with exceptional multi-threaded scale, making it well fitted for large language model fine-tuning, high-throughput distributed inference, computer vision training, and large-scale data science pipelines.
